questions.q_en: A dishonest seller sells rice at a profit of 23% on cost price and wheat at a profit of 20% on cost price. He also uses a measure of 750 gm instead of 1 Kg. Find the percent profit earned by him, if he sells 1 Kg rice and 1 Kg wheat to a customer.
questions.solution_en:
Let, cost price of 1 Kg rice = Rs.100

And cost price of 1 Kg wheat = Rs.100

Total cost price of 1 Kg rice and 1 Kg wheat = Rs.200

Selling price of 750 gm rice = 100 x 123/100 = Rs.123

Selling price of 1 Kg = 1000 gm rice = 123/750 x 1000 = Rs.164

Selling price of 750 gm wheat = 100 x 120/100 = Rs.120

Selling price of 1 Kg = 1000 gm wheat = 120/750 x 1000 = Rs.160

Total selling price of 1 Kg rice and 1 Kg wheat = 164 + 160 = Rs.324

% profit = (324 - 200)/200 x 100

= 124/200 x 100

= 62%

questions.q_en: A dishonest dealer sells his goods at 10% loss on the cost price but uses a faulty weight that weighs 30% less. His profit or loss percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places) is:
questions.solution_en:
The dealer sells goods at a 10% loss based on the cost price.

The faulty weight the dealer uses weighs 30% less than the actual weight.

Let the cost price of the goods be Rs. C

Since the dealer is selling at a 10% loss, the selling price can be calculated as :

SP = C * (1 - 0.10) = 0.90 C

The faulty weighs 30% less, meaning the dealer gives only 70% of the goods.

Effective selling price = SP/0.70 = 0.90C/0.70

=> 9C/7 or 1.2857C

Effective selling price is 1.2857 times the cost price, which means a profit of approximately 28.57%.

questions.q_en: A shopkeeper gives a discount of 10% on the purchase of 10 kg of lentils. the cost price of the lentils is Rs. 40/kg and the marked price is Rs. 45/kg. The weighing machine of the shopkeeper is faulty, and it shows weight of 1 kg when the actual weight is 900 grams. find the percentage profit of the shopkeeper(rounded off to two decimal places).

Cost price of lentils = Rs. 40/kg

Marked price = Rs. 45/kg

Discount given = 10%

The faulty weighing machine shows 1 kg when the actual weight is 900 grams.

SP = MP * (1 - discount percentage) = 45 * (1 - 0.10)

=> Rs. 40.5/kg

Effective selling price for 900 grams of lentils is Rs. 40.5/kg which means the effective selling price per kg (1000 grams) will be :

Effective selling price = 40.5/0.90 = Rs. 45/kg

The profit per kg of lentils is the difference between the effective selling price and the cost price.

Profit/kg = 45 - 40 = Rs. 5/kg

Required profit percentage = 5/40 * 100 = 12.5%

questions.q_en: A retailer cheats his wholesaler and customer both. He purchases (X + 5) % more from the wholesaler and sells (X - 5) % less while selling to his customer. Find the value of X, if the profit percentage by selling the goods at cost price is 33(1/3)%
questions.solution_en:
From the statements, he purchases (105 + X) g instead of 100g and he sells (105 - X) g instead of 100 and (105- X) < 100.

Therefore, in the whole transaction he gains = (105 + X - 100) + (100 - 105 + X)

= 5 + X + X - 5 = 2X gm

ATQ,

(2X) * 100/ (105 - X) = 100/3

6X = 105 - X

7X = 105

X = 15.

questions.q_en: Pritam buys rice at the rate of Rs. 15/kg. He sells it to Rhitam at 20% profit. However his faulty balance shows 1 kg when it is actually 850 gm. Rhitam bought 20 Kgs of rice from Pritam. What is the overall profit (in Rs.) that Pritam makes?
questions.solution_en:
Pritam sells rice to Rhitam at a price of = (15+20% of 15)= Rs.18/kg.

Now Rhitam bought 20 Kgs from Pritam at a total price of =Rs. 18*20 =Rs. 360

But as Pritam has a faulty balance thus he is actually selling 850*20/100=17Kgs instead of 20 Kgs.

Pritam buys 17kgs of rice at a total price of =Rs.17*15 =Rs. 255 and sells it to Rhitam at a price of Rs.360

So Total profit that Pritam makes =Rs. (360 - 255) =Rs. 105.
